Marissa — thanks for the recap and the clear next steps. Attaching the 7-day sample you requested (traffic_sample_7d.csv). A few clarifications from our side to help the sizing:

- Product flows: 1) Conversational summarization (avg user session = 2 requests, often pipelined), 2) Embedding-based semantic search (batch and single request patterns).
- Current peak TPS: ~45 TPS for embeddings (batched), ~15 TPS for short-chat generative calls during business hours; sustained baseline is ~8–10 TPS.
- Concurrency: peaks produce ~120 concurrent active users (many short calls), but batching reduces per-request GPU work.
- Token mix: prompts average 120 tokens; completions average 200 tokens for the summarization flow. Embedding requests average 1,024 tokens (we batch up to 64).
- Preferred GPUs: we don't have a hard requirement; cost is a factor. If H100 reduces latency by 30% for our model we are open, but we need pricing impact.
- SLA: 99.9% desired, with <200ms added P99 latency for short-gen calls.

Let me know if you need any other fields in the CSV. Happy to schedule the workshop — our availability next week is Tue/Wed afternoons PST.

Thanks,

Hi Samir / Marissa —

Thanks for the data and the clear breakdown, Samir — this is exactly what we need. A few notes and initial sizing guidance from a serving/infra perspective: 

1) GPU family tradeoffs (short summary):
   - A100 80GB (fp16/llm.int8-friendly): cost-efficient for higher concurrency and batching; good for larger KV caches.
   - H100 80GB: best latency for many transformer workloads, often fewer GPUs needed for tight P99 latency SLOs but at higher hourly cost.
   - L4/H200 (inference-optimized): very cost-effective for smaller models or high-throughput embedding pipelines; check model compatibility.

2) From your numbers:
   - Embedding TPS: peak ~45 TPS batched up to 64 -> suggests a dedicated embedding pool with aggressive batching and high concurrency. 1–2 L4 nodes could handle embedding needs depending on model size/quantization.
   - Generative short-chat: peak ~15 TPS with prompt+completion ~320 tokens total and P99 latency target <200ms added — to hit that P99 we typically recommend H100-backed nodes or an A100 pool with aggressive KV caching and optimized kernels. Expect 1 H100 or 2 A100s for an initial conservative-sized pool (assuming an LLM in the 7–13B family).

3) Concurrency & batching guidance:
   - For conversational gen, set per-GPU concurrency targets of 8–16 depending on batching window (20–50ms).
   - Embedding pool should prioritize larger batch sizes and higher concurrency (32+), with queued batching to maximize throughput.

4) Token mix and cost implications:
   - Average 320 tokens / gen call and 45 TPS batched embeddings are both material to GPU utilization. We'll prepare per-token cost estimates for A100 vs H100 vs L4 for both workloads.

5) Data isolation and Private path:
   - Since you have PII in logs, Dedicated with customer-isolated VPC (Redwood Dedicated + private network peering) is the recommended near-term approach. Private on-prem is viable later for regulated customers but has longer lead times.

Next step recommendations before the workshop:
   - If you can: (a) confirm the model families you plan to run (open-model name/version), (b) share 24–72h higher-fidelity tail-latency samples (P50/P90/P95/P99) and any cold-start patterns.
   - We'll run a quick throughput sim and bring two concrete sizing options to the workshop: (A) Latency-optimized (H100-lean) and (B) Cost-optimized (A100/L4 mix).

I'll prepare a short slide (2–3 pages) with expected GPU counts, concurrency targets, and rough monthly committed pricing ranges.

—Aditya
